questions.question: The Kopili Hydro Electric Project is located in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kopili Hydro Electric Project** is located in the state of **Assam**, India.
 
• It is developed and maintained by the **North Eastern Electric Power Corporation (NEEPCO)**, which is a public sector enterprise under the Ministry of Power, Government of India.
 
• The project utilizes the waters of the **Kopili River**, which originates from the Meghalaya hills and flows through Assam.
 
• It plays a significant role in meeting the power requirements of the northeastern region of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, and other nearby states.
 
• The hydroelectric project has an installed capacity of approximately **275 MW**, making it one of the critical sources of renewable energy in the region.
 
• The project has faced challenges due to environmental concerns and issues such as water pollution caused by coal mining activities upstream. These issues have impacted the river's water quality, affecting the project's operations.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Assam.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Location of Kopili Hydro Electric Project:**

 
 
• The project is situated in the northeastern state of **Assam**. The river flows through areas of Assam and Meghalaya.
 
• The **Kopili River** serves as the primary source for the project, originating in Meghalaya and flowing into Assam.
 
 
 
• **NEEPCO and its Role:**
 
 
• **North Eastern Electric Power Corporation (NEEPCO)** is responsible for the operation of the Kopili Hydro Electric Project. It is a PSU under the Ministry of Power.
 
• NEEPCO contributes significantly to the power generation in the northeastern region of India, ensuring electricity supply to states like Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, etc.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Challenges:**
 
 
• The **Kopili River** faces pollution issues due to coal mining activities in Meghalaya, which impact the operation of the hydroelectric project.
 
• Efforts are being made by local governments and environmental bodies to address these concerns and ensure sustainable use of the river resources.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Hydroelectric Projects:**
 
 
• Hydroelectric projects like Kopili contribute to **renewable energy generation** and help reduce dependency on fossil fuels.
 
• They are essential for meeting the energy demands of remote and rural areas, particularly in northeastern India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hydroelectric Power in India:**

 
 
• India has significant potential for **hydroelectric power generation**, with projects spread across states like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, and Assam.
 
• Hydropower contributes to **clean energy** and helps the country in its transition towards renewable energy goals.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy Goals:**
 
 
• India aims to achieve a target of **500 GW of non-fossil fuel energy capacity by 2030**, and hydroelectric projects will play a significant role in achieving this target.
 
• The **International Hydropower Association (IHA)** has recognized India's efforts in promoting hydropower as a sustainable energy source.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct descending order of ministerial ranks in the Union Council of Ministers, as per Indian practice?

options.text: Cabinet Minister → Deputy Minister → Minister of State
Minister of State → Cabinet Minister → Deputy Minister
Deputy Minister → Minister of State → Cabinet Minister
Cabinet Minister → Minister of State → Deputy Minister

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cabinet Minister → Minister of State → Deputy Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Union Council of Ministers:** In the Indian parliamentary system, the Union Council of Ministers consists of three categories of ministers: **Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.**
 
• **Cabinet Ministers:** They hold the highest rank and are responsible for major ministries such as Finance, Home, Defense, and External Affairs. They have decision-making power and participate in Cabinet meetings.
 
• **Ministers of State:** They assist Cabinet Ministers and may either handle independent charge of smaller departments or work under Cabinet Ministers for specific portfolios. Their authority is subordinate to Cabinet Ministers.
 
• **Deputy Ministers:** They are the lowest-ranked ministers in the hierarchy. Their role is mainly to assist Cabinet Ministers or Ministers of State in administrative work or specific tasks.
 
• Thus, the correct descending order of ranks is **Cabinet Minister → Minister of State → Deputy Minister**. *Hence, Option 4 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cabinet Ministers:**

 
 
• They head important ministries and are part of the **core decision-making body** of the government.
 
• Examples include **Finance Minister**, **Home Minister**, and **External Affairs Minister**.
 
• Cabinet Ministers discuss and decide on policies, laws, and issues of national importance. They also represent India at international platforms.
 
 
 
• **Ministers of State:**
 
 
• Ministers of State may work independently (with independent charge) or under Cabinet Ministers.
 
• They typically manage smaller departments or specific aspects within major ministries. For example, the Minister of State for Finance may handle taxation issues.
 
 
 
• **Deputy Ministers:**
 
 
• Deputy Ministers support Cabinet Ministers or Ministers of State in administrative and policy-related tasks.
 
• They do not have independent decision-making power but assist in effective governance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Parliamentary System in India:**

 
 
• India follows a **parliamentary system** of governance, where the Prime Minister is the head of the government, and the Council of Ministers is responsible for policy implementation.
 
• The President appoints ministers on the recommendation of the Prime Minister, and they collectively hold responsibility to the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Prime Minister:**
 
 
• The Prime Minister is the leader of the Council of Ministers and decides the portfolios of ministers.
 
• He/she coordinates between different ministries and ensures the smooth functioning of the government.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• The Union Council of Ministers is mentioned under **Article 74 and Article 75** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• Article 75 specifies that the ministers are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: The Bhabar region lies in which part of the Great Plains?

options.text: Adjacent to the foothills of the Himalayas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adjacent to the foothills of the Himalayas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhabar region** is located **just adjacent to the foothills of the Himalayas**. This region is a narrow belt of coarse alluvial deposits, mainly composed of boulders and pebbles.
 
• It acts as a transitional zone between the Himalayan foothills and the Terai region. The Bhabar region slopes downwards towards the south, forming a natural barrier for water flow.
 
• The porous soil of Bhabar allows the streams descending from the mountains to disappear underground, making surface water largely absent here. This feature is unique to the Bhabar. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
• **Vegetation:** The region is sparsely vegetated due to its dry soil conditions. It mostly consists of grasses and shrubs, and agricultural activities are minimal.
 
• The Bhabar region plays a crucial role in the hydrology of the area, as it absorbs the surface water from the Himalayas, which then re-emerges in the Terai region. *This highlights its importance in ecological balance.*
 
• Other options such as West of the Indus Plain, Brahmaputra Basin, and South of Terai are incorrect as they do not geographically align with the Bhabar region.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Adjacent to the foothills of the Himalayas.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of the Bhabar Region:**

 
 
• The Bhabar region is a narrow belt, typically 8-16 km wide, stretching along the Himalayan foothills in northern India.
 
• **Soil composition:** It is primarily composed of coarse alluvial deposits, such as boulders, pebbles, and gravel, which have been brought down by rivers originating in the Himalayas.
 
• Due to its porous soil, the region does not retain surface water, which percolates underground to re-emerge in the Terai region further south.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance:**
 
 
• **Location:** The Bhabar region lies at the base of the Himalayas, forming a natural boundary between the mountainous areas and the plains.
 
• **Hydrology:** It acts as a natural filtration zone, absorbing water and ensuring the availability of underground aquifers in the Terai region.
 
• **Vegetation:** Sparse vegetation due to dry soil conditions; grasslands dominate the landscape.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Regions:**
 
 
• The Terai region lies south of the Bhabar and is characterized by marshy lands due to the re-emergence of water absorbed by the Bhabar.
 
• The Indus and Brahmaputra basins are located far from the Bhabar region and have different geographical and ecological characteristics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hydrological Importance:**

 
 
• The Bhabar region ensures underground water recharge for the Terai plains, maintaining ecological balance in the region.
 
 
 
• **Geological Formation:**
 
 
• The region has been formed by centuries of erosion and deposition processes carried out by Himalayan rivers.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**
 
 
• While not agriculturally productive, the region supports ecological stability, making it crucial for sustainable water resource management.

questions.question: Which of the following important Indian festivals was observed on 13th and 14th March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Holi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Holi**, also known as the **Festival of Colours**, is a prominent Hindu festival celebrated with great fervor across India and in many parts of the world.
 
• It is observed on the **full moon day** of the Hindu month of **Phalguna**, which typically falls in March. In 2025, Holi was celebrated on **13th and 14th March**.
 
• Holi signifies the victory of **good over evil**, marking the triumph of Lord Vishnu's devotee **Prahlada** over the demoness **Holika**. Hence, it is a culturally significant event.
 
• The festival is celebrated with various traditions such as **Holika Dahan** (bonfire on the eve of Holi) and the playful throwing of **colored powders** and water on each other.
 
• Holi serves as an occasion for people to come together, bury past grievances, and strengthen social bonds. *Hence, the correct answer is Holi.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Celebration of Holi:**

 
 
• Holi is celebrated in two main phases: **Holika Dahan** and **Rangwali Holi**. Holika Dahan involves lighting a bonfire to symbolize the defeat of evil forces, while Rangwali Holi is marked by the playful throwing of colored powders and water.
 
• People sing, dance, and enjoy festive food such as **gujiya**, **thandai**, and other traditional sweets during the celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Holi is rooted in Hindu mythology, particularly the story of **Prahlada** and **Holika**. Prahlada's unwavering devotion to Lord Vishnu and his survival from the fire set by Holika is celebrated as a victory of faith and goodness.
 
• **Lord Krishna** and his playful use of colors with Radha and the gopis is also associated with the festival, adding a romantic and joyous dimension to Holi.
 
 
 
• **Regional Variations:**
 
 
• While Holi is celebrated throughout India, the traditions differ from region to region. For example, in **Vrindavan** and **Barsana**, Lathmar Holi involves women playfully hitting men with sticks.
 
• In **Bengal**, Holi is celebrated as **Dol Jatra**, focusing on devotion to Lord Krishna and Radha.
 
 
 
• **Global Celebrations:**
 
 
• Holi has become popular in many countries outside India, including the **United States**, **United Kingdom**, and **Australia**, as a celebration of joy, unity, and diversity.
 
• Events such as the **"Festival of Colors"** organized in various parts of the world attract participants from diverse cultures and ethnicities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Holika Dahan:**

 
 
• Holika Dahan is performed on the eve of Holi to signify the burning of evil forces. People gather around the bonfire, chant prayers, and seek blessings for prosperity and health.
 
• The bonfire is often made with wood and dried leaves, symbolizing the end of the cold season and the arrival of spring.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns:**
 
 
• In recent years, awareness has been raised about the environmental impact of Holi celebrations, such as the excessive use of water and harmful chemical colors.
 
• Eco-friendly practices, like using natural or organic colors and conserving water, have been promoted to make the festival more sustainable.

questions.question: Which issue did the World Economic Forum highlight as the top immediate global threat in its 2025 Global Risks Report published in January 2025?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **State-based armed conflict** has been highlighted as the top immediate global threat in the **2025 Global Risks Report** published by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)**. This is due to the increasing geopolitical tensions and conflicts between states globally.
 
• The report emphasizes the rising risks of direct military confrontations between nations, especially in regions such as **Eastern Europe, the Middle East, and the Asia-Pacific**. These conflicts pose significant threats to global stability. *Hence, this is the correct option.*
 
• State-based armed conflicts often have far-reaching consequences, including **humanitarian crises, disruption of global trade, and economic instability**. Such conflicts can also escalate into proxy wars involving multiple countries. *Hence, this is a major global risk.*
 
• The report warns about the compounded risks of **state-based conflicts** with other issues such as climate change, economic instability, and cyberattacks, which could exacerbate the impact of such conflicts. *Therefore, statement is correct.*
 
• The **Russia-Ukraine conflict** is cited as a prime example of state-based armed conflict and its ripple effects on energy prices, food shortages, and strained geopolitical alliances. *Hence, this is a relevant global threat.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF) Global Risks Report:**

 
 
• **The Global Risks Report** is an annual publication by the **World Economic Forum**, analyzing risks that could affect global stability. The 2025 report particularly focuses on geopolitical tensions and their implications.
 
• The report identifies risks in categories such as **economic, environmental, geopolitical, societal, and technological threats**. State-based armed conflict was ranked as the most immediate threat in 2025.
 
 
 
• **Examples of State-Based Armed Conflicts:**
 
 
• **Russia-Ukraine War:** Started in **February 2022**, leading to significant disruptions in global energy markets and food supply chains.
 
• **Middle East Conflicts:** Long-standing conflicts such as the **Israel-Palestine conflict**, the Syrian civil war, and tensions in Iraq continue to destabilize the region.
 
• **Asia-Pacific Tensions:** Escalating tensions between **China and Taiwan**, as well as disputes in the South China Sea, are significant examples of state-based armed conflict.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Armed Conflicts:**
 
 
• Armed conflicts lead to **humanitarian crises**, including displacement of populations, loss of lives, and destruction of infrastructure.
 
• They disrupt **global trade and supply chains**, particularly in sectors such as energy, agriculture, and manufacturing.
 
• Conflicts also exacerbate political instability and can result in **economic recessions** and reduced foreign investments in affected regions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Recommendations by WEF:**

 
 
• The **Global Risks Report** recommends prioritizing **conflict resolution mechanisms**, strengthening international alliances, and enhancing global governance frameworks to prevent state-based armed conflicts.
 
• It emphasizes the need for **multilateral cooperation** to address underlying causes such as resource disputes, political instability, and territorial claims.
 
 
 
• **Broader Implications:**
 
 
• State-based conflicts can have long-term implications on **global economic growth**, with reduced investments and diminished international trade.
 
• They also exacerbate existing global challenges like **climate change, food insecurity, and migration crises**, requiring integrated solutions.
 
• The role of international organizations like the **United Nations** and regional alliances in conflict resolution has been highlighted in the report.

questions.question: The Parthians originated from which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iran**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Parthians originated from Iran:** The Parthians were an ancient Iranian people who established the Parthian Empire, which lasted from **247 BCE to 224 CE**.
 
• The Parthian Empire is also known as the **Arsacid Empire**, named after its founder **Arsaces I**, who started the dynasty in northeastern Iran.
 
• Parthians played a crucial role in ancient history by acting as a cultural and political bridge between the **Roman Empire** and the civilizations of Asia, including the **Silk Road trade network**.
 
• They are famous for their unique military tactics, especially their **horse-mounted archery skills**, which made them formidable opponents in battles against the Romans and other empires.
 
• The Parthians were known for their contributions to **art, architecture, and governance**, blending Hellenistic and Iranian traditions. This cultural synthesis is evident in their coinage, monuments, and administrative practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Location:**

 
 
• The Parthians originated in the region of **northeastern Iran**, primarily in the area known as **Parthia**, which corresponds to modern-day **Khorasan Province**.
 
• Their empire expanded westward to encompass regions of **Mesopotamia**, eastern Anatolia, and portions of the **Caucasus**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Parthians rose to power after overthrowing the **Seleucid Empire**, which itself was a successor of the empire of **Alexander the Great**.
 
• Under the leadership of various rulers, the Parthian Empire became a dominant force in the Middle East, rivaling the **Roman Empire**.
 
 
 
• **Parthian Contributions:**
 
 
• **Art and Architecture:** Parthian art blended **Greek, Persian, and local styles**, evident in their sculptures, pottery, and city designs.
 
• **Military Innovations:** The Parthians were renowned for their cavalry, especially the use of heavily armored horsemen called **cataphracts** and skilled mounted archers who could shoot arrows backward while retreating (the "Parthian shot").
 
• **Economic Importance:** Their empire was a key player in the **Silk Road trade**, facilitating the exchange of goods, ideas, and cultures between East and West.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Parthian Empire:**

 
 
• **Governance:** The Parthians practiced a decentralized form of governance, allowing local rulers to maintain significant autonomy while remaining loyal to the empire.
 
• **Culture:** The blending of Iranian and Hellenistic traditions under Parthian rule set the stage for the development of the later **Sassanian Empire**.
 
• **Military Strategies:** Their military prowess was characterized by the ability to use terrain, mobility, and psychological warfare to defeat their enemies, including the Romans.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The Parthians left a lasting impact on the history of **Iran**, influencing subsequent empires such as the **Sassanian Empire**.
 
• Their contributions to trade, culture, and governance continue to be studied as a significant chapter in ancient world history.

questions.question: Which technology uses acoustic waves to locate objects in the ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sonar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sonar** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) is a technology that uses **sound waves** to detect, locate, and map objects underwater. It operates by emitting sound pulses and measuring the time taken for the echo to return after bouncing off an object.
 
• **Acoustic waves** are the core component of sonar technology. These waves travel through water, hit an object, and reflect back, allowing the system to calculate the object’s location based on the time and speed of sound.
 
• Sonar is widely used for **navigating, mapping the ocean floor, detecting submerged objects like submarines, and conducting scientific research**.
 
• It is especially useful in **marine environments**, where visibility is low, and other technologies like radar do not function effectively underwater due to the attenuation of electromagnetic waves.
 
• Sonar systems are classified into two types: **active sonar** (which emits sound waves and listens for echoes) and **passive sonar** (which only listens for sounds made by other objects). Both play vital roles in underwater navigation and exploration.
 
• The applications of sonar include **military purposes** (submarine detection, mine hunting), **commercial uses** (fish finding, underwater oil exploration), and **scientific research** (mapping oceanic structures).
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Sonar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Technologies Mentioned in the Question:**

 
 
• **Sonar:** Used for underwater exploration, navigation, and object detection. It is highly effective in water where visibility is limited. Applications include military submarines, undersea exploration, and commercial fishing.
 
• **LiDAR:** (Light Detection and Ranging) uses **laser light** to measure distances. It is primarily used for mapping and surveying land-based terrains, not underwater applications, as light cannot penetrate water efficiently.
 
• **Echo-sounder:** A specialized form of sonar used in marine environments to measure the depth of water and locate the seabed. It is commonly used in hydrographic surveys.
 
• **SAR:** (Synthetic Aperture Radar) uses microwave radar technology to create two-dimensional images of objects, such as landscapes or buildings. It is not suitable for underwater object detection.
 
 
 
• **Sonar in Detail:**
 
 
• **Active Sonar:** Emits sound waves and analyzes the echo for distance, size, and shape of the object. Used in military applications like submarine tracking and anti-mine operations.
 
• **Passive Sonar:** Only listens to sounds generated by underwater objects. Widely used in detecting marine life, ships, and submarines.
 
• **Key Applications:** Includes ocean floor mapping, fish population tracking, underwater archaeology, and disaster management (e.g., detecting underwater earthquakes).
 
 
 
• **Important Characteristics:**
 
 
• Sonar technology is reliable in underwater environments due to the efficient propagation of sound waves in water compared to electromagnetic waves (used in radar).
 
• The speed of sound in water is approximately **1500 meters per second**, allowing accurate calculations of object distance and location.

questions.question: To control over district courts and subordinate judiciary lies with which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High Court**__.

__
 
• **Control over district courts and subordinate judiciary:** According to the **Indian Constitution**, the **High Court** exercises supervision and control over district courts and subordinate judiciary within its territorial jurisdiction.
 
• This includes administrative control, disciplinary measures, and ensuring efficient functioning of subordinate courts. *Hence, the High Court is the correct authority.*
 
• **Article 227:** It gives the High Court the power of superintendence over all courts and tribunals in its jurisdiction, except military courts. *This ensures accountability and proper administration of justice.*
 
• The High Court can also call for records and reports from subordinate courts, issue directions, or transfer cases as deemed necessary. *Hence, the High Court has complete administrative control.*
 
• While other institutions like the **President of India, State Government, and Supreme Court** play significant roles in governance, the High Court is specifically designated to oversee the functioning of district and subordinate courts. *Hence, they are not directly responsible for this control.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 227 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• **Article 227** establishes the supervisory role of the High Court over all subordinate courts and tribunals within its jurisdiction.
 
• The High Court ensures the proper functioning, accountability, and adherence to judicial procedures in these courts. It can issue directions, transfer cases, and monitor their performance.
 
 
 
• **Role of the High Court:**
 
 
• The High Court has the authority to appoint, transfer, and take disciplinary action against subordinate judges. It ensures that the judiciary operates without bias and complies with established norms.
 
• The High Court plays a crucial role in maintaining the independence of the judiciary by safeguarding against external interference.
 
 
 
• **Other Authorities and Their Roles:**
 
 
• **President of India:** The President appoints judges to the High Court and Supreme Court but does not exercise direct control over district courts.
 
• **State Government:** The state government provides administrative support and resources to the judiciary but does not control subordinate courts.
 
• **Supreme Court of India:** As the apex court, the Supreme Court can hear appeals from High Courts, but it does not have supervisory control over district and subordinate courts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Judicial Independence:**

 
 
• The independence of judiciary is a cornerstone of democracy. The High Court ensures this by managing subordinate courts free from executive interference.
 
• The judiciary operates based on principles of fairness, impartiality, and adherence to the rule of law.
 
 
 
• **Example of High Court Supervision:**
 
 
• For instance, the High Court can intervene in cases of judicial misconduct or inefficiency in subordinate courts.
 
• It can also direct lower courts to expedite pending cases or follow proper legal procedures.

• This special majority ensures that amendments to the Constitution are passed with significant support, making the process rigorous and reflective of widespread consensus. *Hence, option 4 is correct.*
 
• Statements like a **simple majority** or a **two-thirds majority of one House** alone are incorrect, as the Constitution requires a more stringent procedure for amendments. *Hence, options 1, 2, and 3 are incorrect.*
 
• The requirement of a **unanimous vote** is impractical and not prescribed for any Constitutional amendment. *Hence, option 3 is incorrect.*
 
• ***Thus, the correct answer is option 4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 368 of the Constitution:**

 
 
• **Article 368** provides the procedure for amending the Constitution. There are two types of amendments: **by a special majority** and **by a special majority with ratification by half of the states**.
 
• It ensures a balance between flexibility and rigidity, safeguarding the Constitution's sanctity while allowing scope for changes.
 
 
 
• **Special Majority:**
 
 
• Special majority refers to **two-thirds of members present and voting** and a **majority of the total membership** of the House.
 
• This provision ensures that amendments are passed with a significant consensus among lawmakers.
 
 
 
• **Types of Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• **Amendments requiring a special majority:** These amendments are passed solely by Parliament through a special majority.
 
• **Amendments requiring ratification:** Some amendments require approval by at least half of the state legislatures in addition to a special majority in Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments:** Introduced provisions for Panchayati Raj Institutions and urban local bodies, passed with a special majority and ratification by states.
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST) Amendment:** Required ratification by states as it altered the federal structure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Provisions:**

 
 
• The procedure for amending the Constitution is outlined under **Part XX** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Amendments cannot be made arbitrarily and require a significant consensus among lawmakers, ensuring democratic process and representation.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• Constitutional amendments play a vital role in adapting the Constitution to changing socio-economic and political realities.
 
• They have been used to introduce key reforms, such as reservations, fundamental rights expansions, and structural changes like GST.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the North Western Railway zone located?
questions.solution:

• It includes major divisions such as **Jaipur, Ajmer, Bikaner, and Jodhpur**. These divisions are strategically located to ensure smooth railway operations in the northern and western parts of India.

• The zone plays a crucial role in facilitating **economic activities**, including the movement of goods and agricultural produce within and outside Rajasthan. *Thus, the importance of Jaipur as the headquarters is undeniable.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Indian Railways:**

 
 
• **Indian Railways** is one of the largest railway networks in the world, comprising 18 zones. It plays a critical role in the transportation of people and goods across the country.

• **About Jaipur:**

questions.question: Which of the following zones receives vertical rays of the Sun throughout the year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical Zone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tropical Zone**, located between the **Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N)** and the **Tropic of Capricorn (23.5°S)**, is the region that receives the **vertical rays of the Sun** throughout the year.
 
• The Sun's rays fall directly over this region during different times of the year due to the Earth's axial tilt and its revolution around the Sun.
 
• This phenomenon creates warm temperatures and leads to the formation of a tropical climate characterized by high temperatures and abundant rainfall. *Hence, the Tropical Zone receives vertical rays of the Sun throughout the year.*
 
• Regions within the Tropical Zone include parts of **South America, Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Indian subcontinent**. These areas experience phenomena like the equatorial climate and monsoons.
 
• Other zones, such as the **Frigid Zone**, **Temperate Zone**, and **Polar Zone**, do not receive vertical rays of the Sun due to their geographical positioning and the Sun's inclination.
 
• The **Frigid Zone** experiences extreme cold due to the Sun's rays falling at a very low angle. Similarly, the **Temperate Zone** receives oblique rays, leading to moderate climates.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Tropical Zone.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zones of Earth:**

 
 
• Earth is divided into different climatic zones based on the angle at which sunlight strikes the surface. The primary zones are the **Tropical Zone, Temperate Zone, Frigid Zone, and Polar Zone**.
 
• **Tropical Zone:** Extends from 23.5° north latitude to 23.5° south latitude. It experiences **direct sunlight** throughout the year and has a warm climate. Regions include the Amazon rainforest, the Congo basin, and Southeast Asia.
 
• **Temperate Zone:** Found between the Tropics and Polar regions, this zone experiences moderate temperatures. Examples include much of Europe, the United States, and southern parts of South America.
 
• **Frigid Zone:** Located near the poles, this zone experiences cold climates and low Sun angles, such as parts of Canada, Greenland, and Antarctica.
 
• **Polar Zone:** Found beyond 66.5° latitude (Arctic and Antarctic Circles), it experiences extreme cold and long periods of sunlight or darkness depending on the season.
 
 
 
• **Phenomena in the Tropical Zone:**
 
 
• The **Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)** is a belt of low pressure that encircles Earth near the equator. It results in heavy rainfall and tropical storms.
 
• The Tropical Zone is also home to major ecosystems such as rainforests, which support high biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Climate:**
 
 
• The direct sunlight in the Tropical Zone results in higher temperatures, which influence weather patterns globally.
 
• Regions here often experience **monsoons** due to differential heating and cooling of land and water.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Characteristics of Climatic Zones:**

 
 
• **Tropical Zone:** Warm temperatures, abundant rainfall, and high biodiversity. Examples include the **Amazon Rainforest** and the **Congo Basin**.
 
• **Temperate Zone:** Moderate climates with distinct seasons. Examples include much of **Europe** and **North America**.
 
• **Frigid Zone:** Extremely cold climates with limited biodiversity. Examples include the **Arctic** and **Antarctica**.
 
• **Polar Zone:** Characterized by low temperatures, ice caps, and long periods of sunlight or darkness. Examples include **Greenland** and **the North Pole**.
 
 
 
• **Sunlight and Earth's Zones:**
 
 
• The amount of sunlight received by each zone determines its temperature and climate. The **Tropical Zone**, receiving direct sunlight, has the most consistent and warm temperatures.
 
• Other zones receive sunlight at oblique angles, leading to cooler temperatures and varied climates.

questions.question: According to the PLFS Annual Report (July 2023–June 2024), which Indian state made history in 2025 by becoming the first to achieve full literacy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mizoram** achieved full literacy in **2025**, making it the first Indian state to reach this milestone, as reported in the **PLFS Annual Report (July 2023–June 2024).**
 
• The state's commitment to education, supported by effective government policies, community participation, and the use of modern technology, contributed to its exceptional performance in literacy.
 
• **Literacy campaigns** in Mizoram focused on primary education, adult literacy, and inclusion of marginalized communities, ensuring equitable access to education.
 
• The state also emphasized the importance of **mother tongue-based education**, which played a significant role in achieving high literacy rates among its indigenous population.
 
• The **PLFS Annual Report** serves as a comprehensive indicator of various socio-economic metrics, including literacy rates, employment data, and other developmental statistics. Hence, this report confirms Mizoram's achievement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Mizoram:**

 
 
• Located in the northeastern part of India, **Mizoram** is known for its lush green landscapes and vibrant culture.
 
• The state has a population of approximately **1.1 million** (2021 Census) and a literacy rate that exceeded **95%** even before achieving full literacy.
 
 
 
• **PLFS Annual Report:**
 
 
• The **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** is conducted by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation in India.
 
• It collects data on various socio-economic parameters, including **employment, unemployment, labour force participation rates, and literacy levels**.
 
• The report for **July 2023–June 2024** highlights Mizoram’s achievement and provides insights into the state’s social development initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Other States:**
 
 
• **Sikkim:** A small northeastern state with high literacy rates but has not achieved full literacy yet.
 
• **Himachal Pradesh:** Known for its mountainous terrain, this northern state has made significant progress in education but has not reached full literacy.
 
• **Kerala:** Often regarded as the most literate state in India, with a literacy rate of over 96%, but not the first to achieve 100% literacy by 2025 as per the PLFS report.

• **Government Initiatives:**

 
 
• Mizoram implemented several state-sponsored programs, such as **adult literacy campaigns, free education schemes**, and community-driven efforts to improve literacy rates.
 
• Focus on **inclusive education** ensured that children from tribal and marginalized communities received access to quality education.
 
 
 
• **Role of Community:**
 
 
• The active involvement of local communities and non-governmental organizations played a crucial role in Mizoram’s achievement.
 
• Use of **local dialects and culture** in educational content helped bridge the gap in education accessibility.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first state to be formed on linguistic basis after severe agitation and the death of a protester?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Andhra Pradesh** was the first state in India to be formed on a **linguistic basis** after extensive public agitation and demands.
 
• The movement for a separate state for Telugu-speaking people gained momentum after the death of **Potti Sriramulu**, a freedom fighter who died during a hunger strike in **1952**.
 
• Following his death, there were widespread protests and public unrest, leading to the creation of Andhra Pradesh in **1953**. *Hence, Andhra Pradesh was the first state to be formed on linguistic grounds.*
 
• The formation of Andhra Pradesh set a precedent for the linguistic reorganization of states in India, which culminated in the **States Reorganization Act of 1956**.
 
• **Telangana**, although a Telugu-speaking region, was not formed as a separate state until **2014**, when it was bifurcated from Andhra Pradesh. *Hence, Telangana is not the correct answer.*
 
• **Kerala** was formed in **1956** under the States Reorganization Act, but not due to linguistic agitation. Its creation was based on the integration of Malayalam-speaking regions. *Hence, Kerala is not the correct answer.*
 
• **Tamil Nadu**, originally known as Madras State, was reorganized and renamed in **1969**. Its formation was not the result of linguistic protests. *Hence, Tamil Nadu is not the correct answer.*
 
• The creation of Andhra Pradesh marked a significant moment in Indian history, emphasizing the importance of linguistic and cultural identity. *Hence, the correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Potti Sriramulu:**

 
 
• **Potti Sriramulu** was a freedom fighter and Gandhian who played a crucial role in the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• He undertook a **fast-unto-death** demanding a separate state for Telugu-speaking people. His death on **December 15, 1952**, sparked massive protests.
 
 
 
• **Formation of Andhra Pradesh:**
 
 
• Andhra Pradesh was officially formed on **October 1, 1953**, with **Kurnool** as its capital.
 
• It was the first state in post-independent India to be created based on linguistic lines.
 
 
 
• **States Reorganization Act, 1956:**
 
 
• This act reorganized states on linguistic grounds across India, following the recommendations of the **States Reorganization Commission**.
 
• The act led to the formation of states like **Karnataka, Kerala, and Maharashtra**.
 
 
 
• **Telangana Formation:**
 
 
• Telangana was formed as a separate state on **June 2, 2014**, after prolonged agitation and political discussions.
 
• It was carved out of Andhra Pradesh, fulfilling the demand for a separate Telugu-speaking state.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Linguistic Identity:**

 
 
• The formation of Andhra Pradesh was driven by the recognition of **linguistic identity** as a basis for state reorganization.
 
• This concept was later extended to other states, ensuring administrative efficiency and cultural preservation.
 
 
 
• **Precedents in State Formation:**
 
 
• **1956:** States Reorganization Act created several states based on linguistic criteria.
 
• **2000:** The formation of **Uttarakhand, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh** reflected socio-economic and cultural considerations.
 
• **2014:** The creation of Telangana emphasized the importance of regional aspirations.

questions.question: In which of the following groups does hydrogen belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Group 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrogen** belongs to **Group 1** of the **Periodic Table**, which is also known as the **Alkali Metals group**.
 
• Hydrogen is placed in Group 1 because it has a single electron in its outermost shell, similar to other elements in the group like **lithium**, **sodium**, and **potassium**.
 
• Although hydrogen is a non-metal, its electronic configuration resembles that of Group 1 elements. It has an atomic number of **1**, making its electronic configuration **1s¹**.
 
• Hydrogen can lose one electron to form a positive ion (H⁺), similar to alkali metals which form positive ions like Na⁺ or K⁺. *Hence, hydrogen is placed in Group 1.*
 
• Hydrogen exhibits properties similar to alkali metals, such as the ability to form ionic compounds with non-metals, further supporting its placement in Group 1.
 
• However, hydrogen also shares similarities with Group 17 elements (halogens) because it can gain an electron to form H⁻, but its primary placement remains in Group 1. *Hence, hydrogen's placement in Group 1 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Group 1 Elements:**

 
 
• **Group 1** consists of alkali metals like **lithium**, **sodium**, **potassium**, **rubidium**, **cesium**, and **francium**.
 
• All elements in Group 1 have **one electron** in their outermost shell, which makes them highly reactive.
 
• They tend to lose their outer electron to form **unipositive ions** (e.g., Na⁺, K⁺).
 
• Group 1 elements form **ionic compounds** with non-metals and are known for their **low ionization energies**.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Hydrogen:**
 
 
• Hydrogen is the **lightest element** with an atomic number of **1**.
 
• It has a single electron and an electronic configuration of **1s¹**.
 
• Hydrogen is unique because it exhibits properties of both **metals** and **non-metals**.
 
• It can form both **ionic** and **covalent compounds**.
 
• Hydrogen is used in industries for applications like **fuel cells**, **ammonia synthesis**, and **hydrogenation** of oils.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Group 17 Elements:**
 
 
• Group 17 elements are known as **halogens** and consist of **fluorine**, **chlorine**, **bromine**, **iodine**, and **astatine**.
 
• Hydrogen shares some similarities with halogens because it can gain an electron to form an anion (H⁻).
 
• However, unlike halogens, hydrogen predominantly loses its electron to form H⁺, aligning it more with Group 1 elements.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hydrogen's Unique Position:**

 
 
• Hydrogen is not classified as an alkali metal but shares several properties with them.
 
• Its placement in **Group 1** is based on its **atomic structure** and **chemical behavior**.
 
• Unlike alkali metals, hydrogen exists as a diatomic gas (H₂) under standard conditions.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Applications of Hydrogen:**
 
 
• **Ammonia production:** Used in the **Haber process** to synthesize ammonia for fertilizers.
 
• **Fuel:** Hydrogen is used in **fuel cells** to generate electricity and is considered a clean energy source.
 
• **Rocket fuel:** Liquid hydrogen is used as a propellant in space exploration.
